questions.question: Which tool would you use to measure a pencil, a tree trunk around its middle, and a school field? Explain.
questions.expected_answer: A ruler for the pencil, because it is short. A tape measure for the tree trunk, because it bends around curves. A trundle wheel for the field, because it measures long distances, clicking once every metre.

questions.question: A pencil ends at the fourth small mark after 12 cm. How long is it in cm and mm, and in mm only?
questions.expected_answer: It is 12 cm and 4 mm long. Each centimetre is 10 mm, so 12 cm is 120 mm, and 120 plus 4 is 124 mm.

questions.question: Order these jumps from shortest to longest: 2 m 35 cm, 2 m 8 cm, 1 m 98 cm, 2 m 50 cm.
questions.expected_answer: Compare the metres first, then the centimetres: 1 m 98 cm, 2 m 8 cm, 2 m 35 cm, 2 m 50 cm.
